items.title: 6.7.1 Relation between enthalpy change and calorie content

source_refs.note: Topic 6.7.1, printed page 126, with the 'Remember' caption of the energy-balance picture (the picture is not reproduced).

blocks.text: The enthalpy of combustion of a food (ΔHc) is the calorie content of that food when it is translated or converted into kilocalories per gram.
Look at the energy provided from glucose.
The calorie content of glucose can be calculated as follows: First, we find ΔH per gram of glucose. Molar mass of glucose is 180gmol⁻¹. Above equation shows that;
mol (180.0 g) of glucose burns to produce energy = 2803 kJ

blocks.text_alt: 1.0 g of Glucose = 2803 kJ/g ÷ 180 g/mol = 15.57 kJ/g

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The heat from one mole is 2803 kJ mol⁻¹, so per gram ΔH = –2803 kJ mol⁻¹ ÷ 180 g mol⁻¹ = –15.57 kJ g⁻¹ (the numerator is kJ/mol, not kJ/g). Putting ΔH = –15.57 kJ/g into the relation gives calorie content = –(–15.57) ÷ 4.184 = +3.72 kcal/g; the printed minus sign comes from dropping the sign of ΔH.
Remember, the calorie content we take from food must be balanced by working, exercising and doing positive activities. Otherwise, our bodies will have imbalanced growth and maintenance
